sb_prompt: WHAT HOBBIES DO YOU HAVE IN YOUR SPARE TIME?  DO THEY INCLUDE ANY HANDICRAFTSWOODWORKING?
turns: So, I guess I'm just into reading and bookbinding; I've always liked putting things together myself.

Oh, that's really cool. I've never tried binding a book myself. I work in a pharmacy, so I'm pretty handy with needles and thread for packaging, but I've never actually made something like that. How did you even get started with it?
Well, it's just always seemed like something satisfying to do with old books, you know?

Yeah, it makes sense when you think about it, but honestly, I'd never trust myself with old paper. My cousin works in archives and she's seen people ruin pages trying to fix them. Do you have to use special thread for it?
Not really, I usually just use regular sewing thread or maybe some heavy-duty linen stuff.
Oh, really? That sounds way less intimidating than using archival tape. Do you think you can make a full hardcover out of it, or mostly just sew the pages together?
Yeah, mostly just sewing the pages together with a little cover slapped on, but I can definitely do a full hardcover if I find some nice leather scraps.
That sounds manageable, though I'm still scared of messing it up if I don't have the right materials.
Yeah, honestly most of my stuff is just old leather I found in thrift stores that I've already cut up, so I don't have to buy anything fancy.
That actually sounds like a great way to start, thrift store stuff probably has the character I'd want.
I mean, I mostly just cut up old wallets and shoe laces to make the covers, so it's pretty low risk.
That's actually really clever, using old wallets and all. Do you have any specific books you're thinking of restoring, or are you just doing random ones for fun?
Just random stuff for now, maybe some old travel guides or novels I've read a hundred times.
That sounds perfect for practice. Do you usually just glue the covers on, or do you actually sew the spine first?
Mostly sew first to hold it together, then glue the cover on, but honestly I'm still figuring out the perfect way to attach the leather without damaging the spine.
That makes sense, I guess if the leather shrinks it'll just pull the spine apart, and my cousin said she avoids glue completely when she fixes patient files.
Yeah, glue is definitely risky since leather shrinks differently than paper, so I've been trying a knot technique instead to keep the spine flexible.
That's clever, avoiding glue sounds way safer than fighting with shrinking material.
Yeah, it keeps the leather breathing a little bit better than the glue would.
That's really smart, keeping it flexible has to be way better for the book in the long run.
Yeah, so far it's holding up okay, though I did have to tighten the first knot twice before it felt right.
That's a relief, I was worried it would snap like a rubber band if I stretched the leather too much.
Yeah, it did stretch a bit when I first pulled it tight, but once I let it rest for a day it settled down pretty nicely.
Yeah, that resting time probably really helps set the tension right.
Yeah, it definitely gets a bit stiff if you leave it on for too long before the glue sets.
Yeah, I think I'm gonna try the knot thing with some old belts I have at home instead of buying new stuff.
That's a great plan, and maybe I should show you how I tie the first knot sometime if you want to try.
That sounds like a really nice gesture, I'd love to see how you tie it.
Yeah, sure, I can send you a quick video showing the first knot if you want.
That'd be awesome, thanks for offering!
Yeah, no problem, I'll just drop you a link tonight.
You got it, I'll look out for it.
You know, that's probably the best way to keep it flexible, though I should mention I usually just thread the needle myself since I don't have any fancy bobbins lying around.
That's a smart hack, threading the needle yourself saves so much money and hassle.
Yeah, honestly I just grabbed a pair of sharp embroidery scissors from the kitchen drawer so I don't even have to run out to the craft store.
Yeah, sharp scissors make all the difference when you're trying to cut thin leather without snipping the thread.
Yeah, I did end up slicing a corner off an old coaster to get the perfect thickness.
That's actually a smart way to get the thickness without buying special foam.
